subject.title: [Bug]: non_deliverable_terminal_turn produces no outbound notification to channel plugins — Octo (and other channels) go silent

question: Should OpenClaw handle `non_deliverable_terminal_turn` for channel plugins by automatically pushing a core fallback through outbound delivery, by adding a public plugin SDK terminal-failure hook, or by leaving the behavior plugin-owned?
rationale: Both viable fixes change user-visible delivery semantics, and the hook option changes the public plugin API, so automation should not choose the permanent owner boundary.

options.title: Core automatic fallback
options.body: Core treats non-deliverable terminal turns as a generic terminal failure and sends the fallback through the existing outbound path so current plugins get protection by default.

options.title: Plugin SDK terminal hook
options.body: OpenClaw adds a documented hook so channel plugins can render their own terminal-failure copy, trading control for opt-in implementation work.

options.title: Plugin-owned workaround
options.body: Core leaves the contract unchanged and asks Octo and other plugins to inspect or recover their own terminal-failure cases.

recommendation.title: Core automatic fallback
recommendation.body: Core treats non-deliverable terminal turns as a generic terminal failure and sends the fallback through the existing outbound path so current plugins get protection by default.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest adjacent history ties this decision to silent-turn fail-closed behavior and outbound reply routing.
